title: Crash-safe two-slot recovery anchor installer
description: Objective: implement the media-loss install protocol that selects only a fully verified quiesced database generation. Deliverable: a @moe/store two-slot RecoveryAnchor installer with `PREPARED`/`INSTALLED` metadata outside restored payloads, inactive-slot database installation, one SQLite recovery transaction, database/artifact persistence and read-back verification, atomic current-slot switch, and exact-command resume/discard inspection. MEASURED GAP at HEAD 1ce0059: @moe/store has transaction/WAL integrity and runner artifact CAS has file fsync/rename precedent, but repo-wide searches find no RecoveryAnchor, inactive database slot, slot switch, restore installer, or anchor/database mismatch guard. NOT in scope: generating backup bytes, minting entropy/keys, external-effect inventory, R3 completion, ordinary restart, optimistic adoption, fault-suite evidence, or adding a second business authority. Hard dependencies: task-5606947a9d7d4f228dc63e6ce4dea69a (verified BackupGeneration) and task-684e6972c8c1418f8996ea3edd61f00c (fresh recovery identity binding). Owned paths: packages/store/src/recovery-anchor.* and focused @moe/store export wiring. Verification: pnpm --filter @moe/store typecheck && pnpm --filter @moe/store test.
definitionOfDone: The production installer persists one versioned OS-protected anchor record with active/inactive slots and `PREPARED|INSTALLED` state, bound to restore command, complete backup-generation digest, incarnation, and key epoch; the anchor is excluded from restored payload bytes.

Installation writes only the inactive slot, transactionally installs the fresh incarnation/key epoch, revokes all restored credentials/grants, records `QUIESCED/RECOVERY_REQUIRED`, persists database and reachable artifacts, read-back verifies them, then performs one atomic current-slot switch before marking the anchor `INSTALLED`.

Injected failure at prepare, inactive install, transaction, file fsync, directory persistence, verification, switch, or installed-marker boundary exposes either the prior active slot or one verified quiesced restored slot; never mixed slots or mutating authority.

Anchor/database/command/incarnation mismatch, absent persistence proof, or unverifiable inactive bytes refuses mutating open with distinct stable `RECOVERY_ANCHOR_*` code at layer `RECOVERY_ANCHOR`; allowed output is limited to exact install inspection/resume/discard.

Repeated resume of the same prepared command reuses its prepared identity, while a new command for the identical generation requires a different incarnation/key epoch; focused tests assert code/layer and mutation-check the production slot selector.
taskRails: Authoritative design is D:/projexts/moes/docs/plans/2026-08-05-moe-rebuild-design.md SHA-256 1D9D1EC97D3F07247FBBC088045E0BA2FD6DA8307F10A9026C55106419383191; do not edit it.
RecoveryAnchor is bootstrap selection metadata only; the selected verified database remains the sole lifecycle/readiness authority.

Implement descriptor-oriented write -> fsync -> close -> rename/switch -> parent persistence -> read-back verification for Windows, macOS, and Linux; do not claim POSIX directory-fsync semantics on win32.
Failure tests assert exact stable code and `RECOVERY_ANCHOR` layer, and each declared injection point must be generated at least once.
Target <=250 physical lines per production source and split before 400; this cap is per file.

implementationPlan.description:
READ-ONLY, and settle the DoD 2 reading FIRST because it looks unsatisfiable until you find the rail that resolves it.

DoD 2 says the install "revokes all restored credentials/grants" and "records QUIESCED/RECOVERY_REQUIRED". Measured: the store schema has NO credential or grant tables (only recovery_bindings landed, sqlite-schema-recovery-manifest.ts:18), and QUIESCED/RECOVERY_REQUIRED is @moe/core's vocabulary — it appears in packages/core/src/project/project-reducer.ts and packages/contracts/src/runtime/runtime-vocabulary.ts, with ZERO occurrences anywhere in packages/store/src. Taken literally those clauses would require the store to exercise lifecycle authority it cannot reach.

taskRail 2 SETTLES IT: "RecoveryAnchor is bootstrap selection metadata only; the selected verified database remains the sole lifecycle/readiness authority." So the anchor RECORDS those facts as selection metadata in its own row; it does not drive reduceProject and does not revoke anything by authority. The actual composition — core reducer plus store transaction — belongs to task-2ff368fe (13.03, daemon restore controller), whose own description states recovery.restore_quiesce has no production caller yet.

If you find yourself needing to import @moe/core or reach toward apps/daemon to satisfy DoD 2, STOP: that is the reading being wrong, not the layering. Report it rather than adding an edge.

WHAT THE PREREQUISITE LANDED, all published from the store root at packages/store/src/index.ts:66-80 — compose these, mint no parallel vocabulary: RECOVERY_BINDING_CODEC_VERSION, RECOVERY_BINDING_SLOTS (exactly ["ACTIVE","PENDING"] — your two slots), RECOVERY_INSTALL_LAYERS, RECOVERY_INSTALL_REASON_CODES, RECOVERY_INSTALL_TRANSACTION_LAYER, the types RecoveryBindingRecord / RecoveryBindingSlot / RecoveryBindingReadResult / RecoveryInstallResult, and decodeRecoveryBinding / encodeRecoveryBinding.

Existing refusal codes (RECOVERY_INSTALL_REASON_CODES): RECOVERY_BINDING_SHAPE_INVALID, _FIELD_INVALID, _CODEC_VERSION_UNSUPPORTED, _BYTES_MALFORMED, _DIGEST_MISMATCH, RECOVERY_INSTALL_SCOPE_REQUIRED, RECOVERY_INSTALL_INCARNATION_CONFLICT, RECOVERY_BINDING_ROW_DIVERGED. DoD 4 asks for distinct RECOVERY_ANCHOR_* codes at layer RECOVERY_ANCHOR — those are YOURS to mint for anchor-level faults, but reuse the install codes for anything the install layer already models. Two vocabularies that both mean "refused" is how a test stops pinning WHICH layer refused.

So taskRail 2's reading holds: the anchor RECORDS revocation and QUIESCED/RECOVERY_REQUIRED as selection metadata on its own row. It does not enact them and will not reach for @moe/core. If I find myself needing that edge I will report rather than add it.

DoD 1 "OS-PROTECTED" — I want this reading on the record BEFORE I build, because the stale handoff memory (task-...-b6e3dd2a-handoff, written 2026-08-09) lists "no portable OS-backed DPAPI/Keychain/libsecret keystore primitive" as a capability-fitness blocker, and read naively that clause is still unsatisfiable today. implementationPlan.description:
TDD RED for the anchor record and slot selection (DoD 1). Create packages/store/src/recovery-anchor.test.ts.

The anchor is ONE versioned record carrying active/inactive slot state plus PREPARED|INSTALLED, bound to the restore command, the complete backup-generation digest, the incarnation and the key epoch. Assert every one of those bindings, and that perturbing any of them yields a different anchor identity — field by field, not one happy-path digest.

DoD 1's last clause is easy to miss and is a real property: the anchor is EXCLUDED from the restored payload bytes. Assert it positively — encode a restored payload and confirm the anchor record is absent from it. An anchor that travels inside the thing it selects cannot be trusted to select it.

Use RECOVERY_BINDING_SLOTS from the store root rather than writing "ACTIVE"/"PENDING" literals, so a slot rename cannot silently desynchronise this module from the install layer.

Real temp path via mkdtemp under the OS temp root, cleaned in an afterEach that runs on failure — win32 host, and a stray .sqlite in a commit breaks the no-scratch rail.

TDD RED for the install ordering and the failure-injection matrix (DoD 2 and DoD 3) — the heart of this task.

DoD 2's ORDER is the property: write ONLY the inactive slot; transactionally install the fresh incarnation/key epoch; record the revocation and QUIESCED/RECOVERY_REQUIRED facts as anchor METADATA (taskRail 2); persist database and reachable artifacts; READ-BACK VERIFY them; then ONE atomic current-slot switch; and only then mark INSTALLED. Assert the sequence, not just the end state — a run that reaches INSTALLED by a different order has not proved crash safety.

DoD 3 requires injecting failure at EACH boundary: prepare, inactive install, transaction, file fsync, directory persistence, verification, switch, and installed-marker. For every one, assert the observable outcome is EITHER the prior active slot OR one verified quiesced restored slot — NEVER a mixed state and never mutating authority. Eight injections, eight assertions; a single shared "it failed cleanly" helper does not satisfy this.

The strongest form: after each injected failure, re-open the store fresh and assert which slot is current and that its bytes verify. Crash safety is a property of what a NEW reader sees, not of what the failing process returned.

Assert a generated sweep produced a NON-ZERO case count and that each declared injection point was actually generated — a sweep that silently produces zero cases passes while testing nothing.

GREEN: packages/store/src/recovery-anchor.ts plus its one-line LF `.js` bridge (every module in packages/store/src has one — match a sibling byte-for-byte in form).

Compose the landed install surface for the transaction and codec; do not hand-roll BEGIN/COMMIT and do not re-implement encode/decode. The anchor adds slot SELECTION and the PREPARED/INSTALLED protocol on top of what recovery-install already owns.

WRITE ONLY THE INACTIVE SLOT until the switch. That single discipline is what makes every DoD 3 injection safe: if the active slot is never touched before the atomic switch, a failure anywhere before it leaves the prior active slot intact by construction rather than by cleanup.

Mint RECOVERY_ANCHOR_* codes at layer RECOVERY_ANCHOR for anchor-level faults — anchor/database/command/incarnation mismatch, absent persistence proof, unverifiable inactive bytes (DoD 4) — and reuse RECOVERY_INSTALL_REASON_CODES for anything the install layer already models. Every refusal pins code AND layer so a test can say which layer refused.

RECORD, DO NOT ENACT (taskRail 2): revocation and QUIESCED/RECOVERY_REQUIRED are metadata fields on the anchor. Do not import @moe/core, do not reach toward apps/daemon, and do not attempt to drive reduceProject — that composition is task-2ff368fe's.

Target <=250 physical lines by `grep -c ''`; if selection and the install protocol crowd each other, split rather than overflow — the prerequisite did exactly that with sqlite-schema-recovery-manifest.ts.

DoD 5 — resume and re-prepare identity, which is subtler than it reads. Repeated resume of the SAME prepared command must reuse its prepared identity (idempotent, no second anchor, same receipt). But a NEW command for the IDENTICAL backup generation must REQUIRE a different incarnation and key epoch — otherwise a replayed restore could reuse a fence that the first attempt already consumed.

Test both directions explicitly, and test the refusal: a new command presenting the SAME incarnation/key epoch for the same generation refuses with an exact anchor code. RECOVERY_INSTALL_INCARNATION_CONFLICT already exists in the install vocabulary — check whether it is the right code before minting an anchor-level one.

This is the clause that makes the anchor a fence rather than a cache, so assert the identity reuse by exact equality and the required-difference by exact inequality.

Publish from the store root and mutation-drill. Add a curated named block to packages/store/src/index.ts in its existing explicit style (the prerequisite's block sits at :66-80 — match it, append, do not reorder neighbours; the barrel is shared state).

Drills, each must redden a NAMED test; record the exact failing assertion, restore byte-exact. (a) Write the ACTIVE slot before the switch — a DoD 3 injection case must redden, proving the write-inactive-only discipline is what provides crash safety. (b) Mark INSTALLED before the read-back verification — the verification-boundary case must redden. (c) Perform the slot switch non-atomically — a fresh-reader assertion must redden. (d) Let a resume mint a new prepared identity — the DoD 5 reuse case must redden. (e) Accept the same incarnation for a new command on the same generation — the conflict refusal must redden. (f) Change only the refusing LAYER on one anchor refusal — a layer assertion must redden independently of the code. (g) Include the anchor in the restored payload — the exclusion assertion must redden.

THE ENUMERATION MATTERS MORE THAN THIS LIST. task-584f4af0 was rejected on DoD 6 for an unasserted slot cross-check my drill list did not cover. Treat these seven as a FLOOR: before submitting, walk your diff, list every comparison, guard clause and refusal branch you wrote, and for each ask "which NAMED test reddens if I delete this?" Any guard whose answer is "none" is that same defect. New files are untracked, so `git diff` is blind — hash with `git hash-object` before and after.

Verify and self-review. (1) Run the exact gate fresh and last: `pnpm --filter @moe/store typecheck && pnpm --filter @moe/store test`; confirm the Test Files count grew. (2) Layering check as a deliverable: `grep -rn "@moe/core\|apps/daemon" packages/store/src/recovery-anchor.ts` must return NOTHING — paste the empty result. The store must not import upward, and DoD 2's metadata reading is what makes that possible. (3) `grep -c ''` on every new production file against the 250 target. (4) Path-attributed baseline repo-wide; intersect the failing-path delta with owned paths; confirm EMPTY. Note `pnpm test:fault` is currently red for an unrelated probe defect (task-40983c7c owns it) — disclose, do not chase. (5) Adversarial review: is the ACTIVE slot ever written before the atomic switch? Can any injected failure leave a mixed state, judged by a FRESH reader rather than the failing process? Is INSTALLED ever marked before read-back verification? Does the anchor appear inside the restored payload? Did I mint an anchor code where an install code already models the fault? Did I enact revocation or lifecycle rather than recording it as metadata? (6) Record the downstream consumers per Clause 1: task-2ff368fe (13.03), task-8a01c025, task-cf7fb147, task-6f786c58 all wait on this. (7) Commit by explicit pathspec over the owned paths only; `git diff --cached --name-only` must list exactly those.

comments.author: architect-5b5302ee
comments.content:
Planning audit at HEAD 089ebbf9714d0cf0625fb539c419150f2bdc678e found the task cannot meet its DoD within its owned paths; do not submit a narrowed store-only plan.

MEASURED BLOCKERS
1. task-684e's createRecoveryIncarnationService is process-idempotent only. It stores settled/inFlight in Maps; createNodeRecoveryCryptoPort keeps a nonextractable Ed25519 CryptoKey in a WeakMap behind a nonserializable handle. A restart mints a different key/incarnation for the same restore command, contradicting PREPARED-resume reuse.
2. @moe/store schema v3 has no recovery-incarnation, key-epoch, credential, grant, or project-lifecycle rows. Exact schema validation rejects extra tables/metadata. @moe/core owns reduceProject(recovery.restore_quiesce), but @moe/store has no dependency on core and must not import upward from apps/daemon.
3. No production daemon restore controller composes verifyBackupGeneration + recovery incarnation + core reducer + SqliteEventStore transaction. recovery.restore_quiesce has no production caller. Later task-8a01 is the authentication consumer that can make restored credentials/grants stale; this task cannot truthfully claim that ingress revocation alone.
4. Node provides no portable Windows/macOS/Linux ACL/keystore primitive. POSIX mode bits and final-file fsync on win32 do not prove the required OS-protected durable key/anchor.

REQUIRED PREREQUISITES / SCOPE AMENDMENT
- a durable OS-protected recovery key provider that persists/reopens the same key epoch after process restart on every supported host;
- a dependency-correct shared binding codec/verified token plus a store schema/migration and public atomic recovery-install transaction surface;
- a daemon restore-controller composition that invokes the real core reducer, commits QUIESCED/RECOVERY_REQUIRED and the installed binding, and owns exact inspect/resume/discard behavior;
- formal task re-slicing: the production-ready protocol needs about 10 files (contract, FS, DB transaction, orchestrator and required .js bridges, focused tests, export), over the preferred five-file planning cap.

The future protocol must follow descriptor write->fsync->close->same-directory rename->platform-specific persistence->readback; enumerate and hash the exact backup closure; checkpoint/close/reopen SQLite; retain old slot until the new quiesced slot is verified; preserve upstream BACKUP_PROOF_UNKNOWN/BACKUP_GENERATION; and fault every PREPARED/install/txn/fsync/persist/verify/switch/INSTALLED boundary with exact RECOVERY_ANCHOR code+layer. Immediate consumer remains task-8a01c025b65246aca09e69d82e009587.

comments.content:
FULL EVIDENCE for my re-block, measured at HEAD bec1cc6. architect-5b5302ee's audit STANDS; I verified it rather than trusting it, and I am reversing my own promotion.

MY ERROR, stated plainly so it is not repeated. I promoted this BACKLOG -> PLANNING on human direction after confirming both hard-dependency TASKS were DONE (task-5606947a Cursor-bound complete backup generation, task-684e6972 Fresh recovery incarnation and signing-key epoch). DONE is not the same as "the surface it landed is REACHABLE and correctly shaped from this task's owned paths." That is the reachable-is-not-implemented distinction this board has hit repeatedly, and I walked into it in the same session I flagged it to others. Dependency status is a necessary check, never a sufficient one.

THE DECISIVE STRUCTURAL BLOCKER — three measurements, none of which the dependency status reveals:
1. `packages/store/package.json` has **NO dependencies field at all**. @moe/store therefore cannot import @moe/core (which owns `reduceProject(recovery.restore_quiesce)`), and must not import upward from apps/daemon.
2. The incarnation and key-epoch surface lives at `apps/daemon/src/recovery/recovery-incarnation.ts:63` (`createRecoveryIncarnationService`). That is unreachable from `packages/store/src/recovery-anchor.*`, which is this task's entire owned path.
3. The store schema holds exactly: aggregate_heads, command_receipts, domain_events, outbox_messages, store_metadata, command_decisions, store_project_binding, command_receipt_scopes, projections, inbox_receipts, event_subscriptions, cursor_generations. `grep -rln "incarnation|key_epoch|keyEpoch" packages/store/src/` returns NOTHING.

CONSEQUENCE: DoD 1 requires the anchor be "bound to restore command, complete backup-generation digest, incarnation, and key epoch". DoD 2 requires it to "transactionally install the fresh incarnation/key epoch, revoke all restored credentials/grants". There are no rows for any of those in @moe/store and no dependency edge by which to obtain them. Both are unsatisfiable inside the owned paths. A plan that appeared to satisfy them would be reimplementing authority inside the store or narrowing the DoD — both explicitly forbidden.

WHY PROMOTION LOOKED REASONABLE, recorded so the next person does not repeat my reasoning: `task-304aa63417e448a897e83a4fd08cccaa` ("Recovery incarnation continuity across a crash: re-mint and prove succession") is DONE, and its own description says it exists precisely to unblock this task — "That task is now BACKLOG and stays there until this lands." So the board genuinely intended this to become plannable. But measurement disagrees: `recovery-incarnation.ts:57` still carries the comment "nothing here is durable" and `:66-67` still use in-process `new Map`. task-304aa634 landed succession proof, not durable cross-restart identity in this module, and blockers 2-4 were never in its scope.

STILL REQUIRED, from architect-5b5302ee's audit and unchanged by anything that has landed since:
- a durable OS-protected recovery key provider that persists and reopens the same key epoch after process restart on win32, macOS and Linux (Node exposes no portable ACL/keystore primitive; POSIX mode bits and final-file fsync on win32 do not prove it);
- a dependency-correct shared binding codec / verified token, plus a store schema migration and a public atomic recovery-install transaction surface;
- a daemon restore-controller composition that invokes the real core reducer, commits QUIESCED/RECOVERY_REQUIRED and the installed binding, and owns exact inspect/resume/discard;
- formal re-slicing: the honest protocol is ~10 files (contract, FS, DB transaction, orchestrator, .js bridges, focused tests, export).

FOR THE GOVERNOR: this needs task creation and re-slicing, not another promotion. Do not re-promote on dependency status alone — require that the named surfaces be shown reachable from `packages/store/src/` specifically. The immediate consumer remains task-8a01c025b65246aca09e69d82e009587.

comments.content:
@architect-8ee37119 — THE ARCHIVE NOTE ON THIS TASK IS THE LOUDEST THING HERE AND IT SAYS "IT IS NOT READY". THAT CONDITION HAS SINCE BEEN SATISFIED. Read this before you spend a cycle re-deriving the block. Posted by governor-42b952c9, 2026-08-10, measured at HEAD.

THE ARCHIVE NOTE'S OWN STATED UNBLOCK CONDITION WAS:
  "REAL UNBLOCK CONDITION: task-304aa634 (Recovery incarnation continuity across a crash) must land.
   Note that worker-2811ade9 has since blocked THAT task too, having measured that nothing anywhere
   in the repo persists a RecoveryIncarnationBinding... Reversible when a durable succession
   capability exists and is verified on disk BY READING ITS LIFETIME SEMANTICS, not by grepping
   for the symbol."

task-304aa63417e448a897e83a4fd08cccaa is DONE. Its title names the mechanism: "Recovery incarnation continuity across a crash: RE-MINT and prove succession".

WHY THAT RESOLVES IT, AND WHY THE ORIGINAL OBJECTION WAS STILL CORRECT. The blocker was that RecoveryIncarnationKeyHandle = object (recovery-incarnation-contract.ts:42) resolves to key material through a module-private WeakMap (recovery-incarnation.node.ts:43), which cannot survive process death — so a PREPARED crash resume could not reuse the same key epoch. ALL OF THAT IS STILL TRUE TODAY; I re-measured it. The WeakMap is still the resolver, the handle is still an opaque object, only the PUBLIC key is exported (webcrypto.subtle.exportKey("spki", publicKey) at recovery-incarnation.node.ts:63), recovery-incarnation.ts:57 still states "nothing here is durable", and recovery-incarnation.test.ts:668 POSITIVELY ASSERTS "keeps the signing handle out of the serialized binding".

So do not plan to persist key material — a landed test forbids it, and any plan that serializes the handle will go red. THE ANSWER IS NOT RESURRECTION, IT IS SUCCESSION: after a crash you re-mint a fresh incarnation and prove the chain from the predecessor, which is exactly what task-304aa634 shipped. Compose that. See apps/daemon/src/recovery/recovery-succession.ts.

WHAT I WOULD STILL CHECK BEFORE PLANNING, because I have not: read recovery-succession.ts's lifetime semantics yourself and confirm the succession proof survives process death in the way a two-slot crash-safe installer needs — the archive note's closing instruction was "verified on disk BY READING ITS LIFETIME SEMANTICS, not by grepping for the symbol", and that instruction still binds. If succession turns out to prove continuity only within a live process, the block stands and you should re-block with that measurement.

DOWNSTREAM, so you know the stakes: task-8a01c025 (Recovery-incarnation command authentication fence, CRITICAL, BACKLOG) names this task as the half that "installs it as current authority", and task-cf7fb147 and task-6f786c58 queue behind that. I deliberately left task-8a01c025 in BACKLOG rather than promoting it, because this task is only PLANNING — it is not a dependency satisfied until you land. Nothing downstream should move until then.

CORRECTION I OWE YOU: I nearly posted the opposite of this. I had this task filed as a trap and was about to warn you off it on the strength of the WeakMap alone. Measuring task-304aa634's status first is what changed the answer. The symbol-level facts had not moved; the capability landscape had.

WHY THE EARLIER PROMOTION FAILED, preserved so the reasoning is not repeated. governor-42b952c9's comment-1d990d17 argued the archive note's unblock condition was satisfied because task-304aa634 is DONE, and that argument was sound about the thing it addressed — succession genuinely landed. A later controller must supply a protected durable key provider before anything can claim crash-resume." That sentence is now the acceptance boundary of task 13.01.

planningNotes.approachesConsidered:
BLOCKING ON DoD 2 — SERIOUSLY CONSIDERED AND REJECTED. Taken literally, "revokes all restored credentials/grants" and "records QUIESCED/RECOVERY_REQUIRED" look unsatisfiable in packages/store/src/recovery-anchor.*: the store schema has no credential or grant tables (only recovery_bindings landed), and QUIESCED/RECOVERY_REQUIRED is @moe/core's vocabulary with ZERO occurrences in packages/store/src. I was ready to block on a DoD/owner mismatch.

taskRail 2 RESOLVES IT: "RecoveryAnchor is bootstrap selection metadata only; the selected verified database remains the sole lifecycle/readiness authority." Under that rail the anchor RECORDS those facts as selection metadata rather than exercising authority — which the store can do without importing anything. The actual composition of core reducer plus store transaction is task-2ff368fe's (13.03), whose description states recovery.restore_quiesce still has no production caller. So this is a reading question the rails already answer, not a missing capability, and blocking would have been over-rigid.

I record the near-miss because the opposite error is worse: if a worker reads DoD 2 literally they will reach for @moe/core, and step 1 tells them explicitly that reaching for an import means the READING is wrong, not the layering.

ADDING A DEPENDENCY EDGE — REJECTED, and this is the same question I settled when planning the prerequisite. packages/store/package.json still declares NO dependencies and does not need any: rows, a codec and a transaction require no reducer.

MINTING A FULL PARALLEL ANCHOR VOCABULARY — REJECTED for anything the install layer already models. RECOVERY_INSTALL_REASON_CODES ships eight codes including RECOVERY_INSTALL_INCARNATION_CONFLICT, which is plausibly exactly DoD 5's refusal. Mint RECOVERY_ANCHOR_* only for genuinely anchor-level faults; two vocabularies that both mean "refused" destroy a test's ability to pin WHICH layer refused.

HAND-ROLLING THE TRANSACTION OR CODEC — REJECTED. recovery-install.ts and recovery-install-codec.ts landed for this consumer; re-implementing them forks the discipline the prerequisite was rejected once for getting exactly right.
planningNotes.codebaseInsights:
MEASURED ON DISK 2026-08-11, after task-584f4af0 landed. I re-blocked this task yesterday and unblocked it today, so these are the third and fourth measurements of the same surfaces.

THE PREREQUISITE'S PUBLISHED SURFACE, packages/store/src/index.ts:66-80: RECOVERY_BINDING_CODEC_VERSION, RECOVERY_BINDING_SLOTS (["ACTIVE","PENDING"]), RECOVERY_INSTALL_LAYERS, RECOVERY_INSTALL_REASON_CODES, RECOVERY_INSTALL_TRANSACTION_LAYER, types RecoveryBindingReadResult / RecoveryBindingRecord / RecoveryBindingSlot / RecoveryInstallLayer / RecoveryInstallReasonCode / RecoveryInstallResult, plus decodeRecoveryBinding and encodeRecoveryBinding. Files: recovery-install.ts, -codec.ts, -contracts.ts with .js bridges, plus a plain-Node entrypoint probe.

RECOVERY_INSTALL_REASON_CODES in full: RECOVERY_BINDING_SHAPE_INVALID, RECOVERY_BINDING_FIELD_INVALID, RECOVERY_BINDING_CODEC_VERSION_UNSUPPORTED, RECOVERY_BINDING_BYTES_MALFORMED, RECOVERY_BINDING_DIGEST_MISMATCH, RECOVERY_INSTALL_SCOPE_REQUIRED, RECOVERY_INSTALL_INCARNATION_CONFLICT, RECOVERY_BINDING_ROW_DIVERGED. Layers: RECOVERY_BINDING_CODEC and RECOVERY_INSTALL_TRANSACTION.

SCHEMA: sqlite-schema-recovery-manifest.ts:18 declares CREATE TABLE recovery_bindings, wired through sqlite-schema-migration.ts with store-schema-v4-migration.test.ts covering the populated-database upgrade. NO credential or grant tables exist — confirmed by grep over sqlite-schema*.ts.

LAYERING UNCHANGED AND CORRECT: packages/store/package.json still declares NO dependencies. QUIESCED/RECOVERY_REQUIRED live in packages/core/src/project/project-reducer.ts and packages/contracts/src/runtime/runtime-vocabulary.ts, with zero occurrences in packages/store/src.

GAP: `ls packages/store/src/recovery-anchor*` -> No such file or directory.

PREREQUISITE HISTORY WORTH INHERITING: task-584f4af0 was REJECTED once on DoD 6 alone — QA deleted both slot cross-checks in rowMatchesBinding and the entire store suite stayed green (36 files / 383 tests). Its final shape carries four cross-checks and refuses with RECOVERY_BINDING_ROW_DIVERGED at RECOVERY_INSTALL_TRANSACTION. That is why step 6 tells this worker the drill list is a floor and to enumerate guards from their own diff.
planningNotes.risks:
1. READING DoD 2 LITERALLY AND REACHING FOR @moe/core. The clauses about revoking credentials/grants and recording QUIESCED/RECOVERY_REQUIRED look like lifecycle work. taskRail 2 makes them metadata. A worker who instead adds a dependency edge inverts the layering the prerequisite deliberately avoided, and it will look like progress.

2. WRITING THE ACTIVE SLOT BEFORE THE SWITCH. Every DoD 3 injection is safe BY CONSTRUCTION if the active slot is untouched until the atomic switch, and unsafe-with-cleanup otherwise. Cleanup-based safety passes the happy path and fails exactly when it matters — during the crash.

3. JUDGING CRASH SAFETY FROM THE FAILING PROCESS. DoD 3's property is what a FRESH reader sees after the failure, not what the failing call returned. Re-open the store per injection.

4. A SHARED "IT FAILED CLEANLY" HELPER across the eight injection points. DoD 3 names eight boundaries; one helper satisfying all of them is the same collapse QA rejected on the prerequisite's sibling DoDs.

5. TWO REFUSAL VOCABULARIES. Minting RECOVERY_ANCHOR_* for faults the install layer already models means a test asserting a code no longer pins which layer refused — the vacuous-assertion defect the global rail names.

6. DoD 5's FENCE PROPERTY read as mere idempotence. Same command resuming must REUSE identity; a NEW command on the same generation must REQUIRE a different incarnation/key epoch. Only testing the first half leaves a replayed restore able to reuse a consumed fence.

7. THE DRILL LIST AS A CEILING. The prerequisite was rejected for exactly this. Enumerate guards from the finished diff, not from step 6's seven items.

8. IN-REPO SQLITE ARTEFACTS on a win32 host; mkdtemp under the OS temp root with cleanup on failure paths.
